title: Preserve cache constructor policy without serializing the populated runtime cache
applies_when: A buffered file serializes a reopen recipe rather than its live cache, and cache_options controls bounds or eviction such as maxblocks or trim. The reader can replace its cache implementation after construction.
lesson: Compare the actual public open/read/pickle/reopen path, not just direct cache-object pickling. Excluding populated cache bytes is compatible with preserving the caller's constructor policy: otherwise a round trip can silently reset a bounded cache or change trimming. Retain the original constructor options separately from mutable runtime state, and only reuse them when the effective cache implementation is still compatible. Include position/returned-byte checks, an initially empty reconstructed-cache control and a read-all/cache-replacement control. In the pinned Fsspec case, both synchronous and asynchronous HTTP readers reset maxblocks=2 to32 and trim=False toTrue; the proposed fix preserves options but does not pass BytesCache options to an AllBytes replacement.
avoid_when: This does not establish a serialization contract for every backend or cache. Caller-supplied options can contain data or unpicklable resources; preserving them does not guarantee a small or universally picklable object. Runtime changes to cache policy need a separate contract. Native loopback correctness and proposed tests are not full CI, production performance, maintainer acceptance or a controlled knowledge-benefit experiment.

evidence.note: Pinned implementation constructs the cache with cache_options, but its file reopen recipe omits these consumed options. Source mechanism, not a native test by itself.

Proposed unmerged tests use real loopback HTTP for both implementations. Identical focused native Linux selection has four failing option-preservation cases and five passing controls on baseline, all nine passing on candidate. The controls retain cache exclusion and read-all replacement behavior; not full CI or acceptance.
Earlier merged change intentionally excludes populated runtime caches from file pickles. Do not reverse that design to fix constructor-option loss.
